H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller explicitly has a parent state Move contact link whose internal phases are Move contact link to way-point and Move contact link to goal.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions/commands use threshold-plane crossing, contact-force disappearance, and the BMI hysteresis rule combining probability thresholds with previous-command conditions.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States drive QP objectives, CoM tracking, contact-link tracking, real-time waypoint updates, torque output, and feedback at each control iteration.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper discusses collision/local-minimum trapping and manual BMI unblocking, but does not define a dedicated fault state or global recovery transition.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Top-level FSM states are defined in Section 3, while substate decomposition, threshold guard, waypoint update, and BMI intervention are explained later in Sections 5-6.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as contact-adding and removing-contact are domain-specific, but the paper spells out their controller behavior rather than requiring external rule decoding.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions for Move contact link are distributed in prose: Section 3 gives QP/contact-link behavior, while Section 5 adds waypoint tracking and BMI-based modification.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The BMI command rule changes c_t only under combined probability-threshold and previous-command conditions; waypoint updates also depend on c_t and time case.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: The composite Move contact link mode has parent-level continuous behavior such as CoM tracking, balance, collision avoidance, and torque output beyond its two child targets.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No rule says that any state jumps to a safe state on a fault; the unblocking behavior is scoped to a contact-adding transition.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is one shallow composite state with an expected initial child path from waypoint tracking to goal tracking.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The controller has a small number of threshold/boolean guard conditions, but not three or more rich arithmetic guard families.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Parent-mode continuous behaviors such as balance, collision avoidance, contact-link tracking, and torque output apply across the child substates.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are mostly concrete control effects such as UDP command input, waypoint motion, QP objectives, and torque commands, not abstract publish/log/notify actions.

one_line_pitch: This is a compact but demanding HSM benchmark because one composite contact-transition state mixes continuous parent actions, geometric guards, and BMI-driven waypoint correction.
rationale: The paper provides an explicit hierarchical FSM with a composite Move contact link state and two internal substates. It is action-heavy because each mode drives QP objectives, CoM/contact-link tracking, waypoint updates, and torque output. Its baseline difficulty is high because state/action details are split across sections and the parent composite mode carries continuous behavior that flat Umple-style extraction can easily miss. Fault recovery is weak, so the sample is strongest as a hierarchy/action/guard stress test rather than as a safety-recovery case.
